liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Drums** (3 other sources): A 0:31 patch from the Schoeps source covers a gap in Drums; A 0:38 patch from the Schoeps source is used in Drums [3][6][7]
- **Friend Of The Devil** (2 reviews): Reviewer praises it as a great later-era Friend of the Devil; Reviewer points to Jerry's vocals on Friend of the Devil as especially strong [36][41]
- **Feel Like A Stranger** (1 review): Opening the show with a strong Stranger stood out to this attendee [37]
- **New Minglewood Blues** (1 review): Reviewer calls the Minglewood an all-time version, in a relatively short first set [36]
- **Hell In A Bucket** (1 other source): A 0:07 Schoeps patch repairs the Hell In A Bucket to Deal transition [6]
- **Mississippi Half-Step Uptown Toodeloo** (1 review): Reviewer rates this Half-Step among the best, possibly the best, of the mid-eighties [33]
- **Franklin's Tower** (1 review): Reviewer singles out Franklin's, Saint and The Other One as great performances [31]
- **Saint Of Circumstance** (1 review): Lost Sailor into Saint into Crazy Fingers and the jam is called the show's highlight [36]

## Setlist highlights

- **Crowd/Space**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [43]

## The recordings

- **gd1985-10-29.178836.nak700.wagner.miller.clugston.flac2496** (recommended): audience recording; 20 songs; 147 min [1]
- **gd1985-10-29.164047.akg451.ck8.eaton.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 20 songs; 142 min [3]
- **gd85-10-29.sbd.hinko.21533.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 19 songs; 142 min; rated 4.79/5 by 28 [14]. Said about its sound: Reviewer ranks this among the best soundboards they have heard, calling the show tight; Reviewer says it is among the best-sounding soundboards in circulation, especially the jam out of Crazy Fingers; Reviewer notes the Fox is always hard to beat for sound [31][32][33][35][39][41]
- **gd1985-10-29.178835.nak700.wagner.miller.clugston.flac1648**: audience recording; 20 songs; 147 min [2]

## Around the show

- Attendee calls it the coolest indoor venue they saw the Dead play; ushers let fans gather right at the stage front [32]
- Attendee had an all-access pass via their father and got to say hi to Jerry and Billy [38]
- Attendee recalls the Fox ceiling lit with star patterns, making it feel like being outdoors [40]
- Reviewer notes Brent was rock solid and Phil was prominent [41]
- Mike's microphone sat dead center about 50-60 feet from the stage, with a cable run from the Official Taper's Section, permitted by Dan Healy [7]
- Reviewer is puzzled it was not released as a Dick's Pick, considering it nearly flawless [33]
- Reviewer recommends the Richmond Coliseum show three days later, Dick's Pick 21, as another outstanding one [35]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1985-10-29.178836.nak700.wagner.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Bob Wagner; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Bob Wagner's Master Audience Cassettes; Nakamichi 700 mics > Sony TC-D5M (Maxell XLII-S 90) [1]
- **gd1985-10-29.164047.akg451.ck8.eaton.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Rob Eaton; transferred by Rob Eaton, Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Rob Eaton's Master Audience Cassettes; AKG 451's w/ CK8 shotguns > Sony D5M [3]
- **gd85-10-29.sbd.hinko.21533.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBD > MC > C > DAT > CD > EAC > SHN [14]
- **gd1985-10-29.178835.nak700.wagner.miller.clugston.flac1648**: taped by Bob Wagner; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Bob Wagner's Master Audience Cassettes; Nakamichi 700 mics > Sony TC-D5M (Maxell XLII-S 90) [2]

claims.text: Reviewer ranks this among the best soundboards they have heard, calling the show tight
Reviewer singles out Franklin's, Saint and The Other One as great performances
Attendee calls it the coolest indoor venue they saw the Dead play; ushers let fans gather right at the stage front
Reviewer says it is among the best-sounding soundboards in circulation, especially the jam out of Crazy Fingers
The jam coming out of Crazy Fingers is recommended for appreciating the soundboard's quality
Reviewer rates this Half-Step among the best, possibly the best, of the mid-eighties
Reviewer is puzzled it was not released as a Dick's Pick, considering it nearly flawless
Reviewer notes the Fox is always hard to beat for sound
Reviewer found the soundboard crystal clear compared with the second-set audience-era tape they had cherished for nearly twenty years
Reviewer recommends the Richmond Coliseum show three days later, Dick's Pick 21, as another outstanding one
Lost Sailor into Saint into Crazy Fingers and the jam is called the show's highlight
Reviewer calls the Minglewood an all-time version, in a relatively short first set
Reviewer praises it as a great later-era Friend of the Devil
Opening the show with a strong Stranger stood out to this attendee
Attendee had an all-access pass via their father and got to say hi to Jerry and Billy
Reviewer says this upgrade has noticeably less high-end hiss than the earlier circulating recording
Attendee recalls the Fox ceiling lit with star patterns, making it feel like being outdoors
Reviewer finds the sound superior, with Jerry's vocals very strong for this period
Reviewer points to Jerry's vocals on Friend of the Devil as especially strong
Reviewer notes Brent was rock solid and Phil was prominent
The Wheel space is included in the track
Rob Eaton made the recording and the transfer; Charlie Miller coordinated, using AKG 451 microphones
A 0:31 patch from the Schoeps source covers a gap in Drums
A 0:07 Schoeps patch repairs the Hell In A Bucket to Deal transition
A 0:38 patch from the Schoeps source is used in Drums
Mike's microphone sat dead center about 50-60 feet from the stage, with a cable run from the Official Taper's Section, permitted by Dan Healy
Drums has a fade out and in at 2:20 caused by a tape flip
